title: Do EV Batteries Die After a Few Years? The Data Says No 🔋📊 #shorts

scenes.text: Myth: an electric car's battery dies after a few years, just like an old phone. The data says otherwise.
Telematics firm Geotab tracked almost five thousand EVs. On average, their batteries lost about one point eight percent of capacity per year.
At that rate, a twelve year old pack would still hold nearly eighty percent.
Recurrent looked at over twenty thousand EVs. For models from twenty sixteen on, one percent or less ever needed a new pack.
Why better than a phone? EVs use liquid cooling, and hide spare capacity at the top and bottom of the charge.
The battery may outlast the car. So what should we do with it next? Follow EV Drive for daily car tech.
